hook.line: On the coast everyone has a dream waiting: a boat, a farm, a quieter life. Spanish has two easy ways to say it, and one small word that English speakers get wrong.
hook.es: Sueño con tener mi propio barco.
hook.en: I dream of having my own boat.

examples.es: Sueño con vivir junto al mar.
examples.en: I dream of living by the sea.

examples.es: Mi sueño es tener una finca.
examples.en: My dream is to have a farm.

examples.es: Yesid sueña con tener su propio barco.
examples.en: Yesid dreams of having his own boat.
I used to dream of a big house.

examples.es: Mariana sueña con escribir un libro.
examples.en: Mariana dreams of writing a book.
What do you dream of? (to a friend)

rule:
To say what you dream of, use *soñar con*, and always *con*: *sueño con vivir junto al mar*. English says *dream of*, but *de* is wrong here.

After *con* comes a verb in the infinitive or a noun: *sueño con viajar*, *sueño con una casa*.

*Soñar* changes its vowel like *poder*: *sueño*, *sueñas*, *sueña*, *soñamos*, *sueñan*.

The other way: *mi sueño es* + infinitive. *Mi sueño es abrir otro café.*

Both work for night dreams too: *Anoche soñé con Rosa.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this a verb with a fixed preposition (*verbo preposicional*): *soñar* always comes with *con*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *con* or *de* and type the whole sentence: *Sueño ___ vivir junto al mar.* (I dream of living by the sea.)
yourTurn.answer: Sueño con vivir junto al mar.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *sueño* or *soño* and type the whole sentence: *Yo ___ con tener un barco.* (I dream of having a boat.)
yourTurn.answer: Yo sueño con tener un barco.
yourTurn.why: The vowel changes in the *yo* form: *o* becomes *ue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: My dream is to have a farm.
yourTurn.answer: Mi sueño es tener una finca.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Mariana dreams of writing a book.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana sueña con escribir un libro.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: What do you dream of? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Con* stays in front of *qué*, because it belongs to the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about *we*: *Sueño con volver a Santa Marta.*
yourTurn.answer: Soñamos con volver a Santa Marta.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it past, like a childhood dream: *Sueño con una casa grande.* (I used to dream of a big house.)
yourTurn.why: *Soñaba* is the ordinary *used to* past, still with *con*.

pitfalls.wrong: Sueño de vivir junto al mar.
pitfalls.right: Sueño con vivir junto al mar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says *dream of*, but Spanish says *dream with*: *soñar con*.
The vowel changes when the stress falls on it: *sueño*, but *soñamos*.

pitfalls.wrong: Mi sueño es de tener una finca.
pitfalls.right: Mi sueño es tener una finca.
pitfalls.why: After *es*, go straight to the infinitive. No extra word.

personal: Tell us what you dream of: *Sueño con…* or *Mi sueño es…*. Something true about you.
